Synopsis:
The player can attempt to vandalize the portrait and can be caught by a nearby gith teenager.

Cluster Contexts:
- CRE_General_VlaakithPortrait.json: You're in the gith crèche before a grand portrait of Queen Vlaakith; Lae'zel stands nearby, reverent toward Vlaakith and openly hostile to any mention of Orpheus. Off-screen you have already met the gith youth (Varrl) and know he’s been secretly reading outlawed writings about Orpheus. Depending on prior choices Varrl may be unharmed and persuadable (able to hand over part of chapter 2), or he may be injured from an earlier fight in which case you can either steal the chapter or heal him before continuing. The player can attempt to vandalize the portrait (for example by drawing a new face) and the nearby Varrl may catch you—he admires Orpheus, fears reprisals for speaking his name, and will respond with gratitude if you show him compassion.
- CRE_PortraitKid.json: A githyanki teenager standing near a portrait of Vlaakith.
- CRE_ChainOfCommand_Templar.json: The inquisitor demands the Orpheus artefact. The player can ask questions or attempt to hand over the artefact, which leads to Vlaakith appearing through the planecaster. Vlaakith explains that there's a prisoner inside who needs to be killed for the safety of the gith and teleports the player into the Astral Prison. Alternatively the player can kill the inquisitor and prompt Vlaakith’s appearance themselves.
- DEN_DruidLair_FrescoVictory.json: In a well-lit cave. Player looks at a fresco depicting a group of druids standing over a vanquished army. Pass a test to realise that the army was the army of Shar - a Dark Goddess.
- CRE_ChainOfCommand_Vlaakith_OM_Laezel_COM.json: Vlaaktih appears as a hologram and Laezel meets her for the first time. Avatar can decide if she accepts her orders to kill the prisoner or refuse. In both cases, the planecaster is activated.If you refuse, Vlaakith orders the inquisitor if alive to kill you if you try to exit the room or theatens to hunt you down if he's already dead. If Laezel is not yet convinced to side with the player, they have a chance to do it here if they refuse.

context: You're in the gith crèche, standing before a grand portrait of Queen Vlaakith with Lae'zel nearby, reverent toward Vlaakith and openly hostile to any mention of Orpheus. Off-screen you have already met the gith teen Varrl, who has been secretly reading outlawed writings about Orpheus; depending on prior choices he may be unharmed and persuadable (able to hand over part of chapter 2) or injured from an earlier fight (in which case you could steal the chapter or heal him). The player can attempt to vandalize the portrait (for example by drawing a new face) and Varrl may catch you — he admires Orpheus, fears reprisals for speaking his name, and will respond with gratitude if you show him compassion. This scene also sits within a larger chain of events around Vlaakith and a planecaster/inquisitor, so confrontation here can feed into later escalations.
